# Claresso â€” Smart Work/Personal Classifier + Humane Personal-Usage Limit

**Final design document Â· v1 scope-locked**

---

## 1. TL;DR

Two problems, one pipeline, joined so that **limiting can never punish a misclassification**.

**Classifier â€” "Provenance Ledger."** A deterministic, content-free cascade in which the *only* signals allowed to auto-resolve a session to **WORK** are **out-of-band-verifiable** (a real git push to a corporate org; a *signed* commit whose IdP-provisioned key identity matches the corporate directory). Everything dev-mutable â€” `git config user.email`, private-registry fingerprints, ticket keys, monorepo walk-up â€” is a **corroborator** that can mark a session **WORK-PROVISIONAL** but never silently auto-classify it. The optional LLM is a **content-tier judge that can only rescue a session toward work, never flag it personal.** Sessions with no work signal sit in a terminal-safe **UNCLASSIFIED** state and surface to a contestable review queue. **PERSONAL is only ever reached by an affirmative personal signal confirmed by two independent signals** â€” so new/separate/remote-less work is never silently flagged personal *by construction*, not by a tunable weight.

**Limiter â€” "Co-Owned Ledger."** v1 is **transparency + reciprocal visibility + a dev-first contestable record**, not enforcement. The cap denominator is **session-count / wall-clock fraction** ("estimated split, not billed dollars"), because the JSONL token fields are a streaming placeholder that undercounts input by **100â€“174Ã—** and output by **10â€“17Ã—** ([gille.ai](https://gille.ai/en/blog/claude-code-jsonl-logs-undercount-tokens/); [anthropics/claude-code#22686](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/22686); [ccusage#866](https://github.com/ryoppippi/ccusage/issues/866)) â€” a dollar meter on that data fires on fiction. Dollars appear **only** as a lagged daily org rollup for the CFO. The UX is allowance-framing + soft friction + one-tap "this is work," surfaced to the dev **before** any manager aggregate. **Hard enforcement is not a v1 capability**; it is a separately-priced, off-device API-proxy SKU, because on-device hooks cannot reliably block (deny-bypass bugs below).

**Honest label:** *v1 is a "classification + transparency + contestable ledger" analytics product.* The words "limit," "cost cap," and "enforcement" attach only to the later proxy SKU, after it passes its own published GO/NO-GO precision gate.

## 2. Smart Work/Personal Classifier

### 2.1 Design principle: trust tiers, not cost tiers

Modern DLP/insider-risk tooling (Microsoft Purview, Forcepoint, Code42/Incydr, DTEX, Cyberhaven) has moved decisively from single-signal rules to **layered contextual signals**, because role-blind single rules are the documented root cause of developer false positives and alert fatigue ([DTEX/Gartner](https://www.dtex.ai/blog/gartner-market-guide-for-dlp-why-context-is-king/); [Cyberhaven](https://www.cyberhaven.com/blog/dlp-false-positives)). Code42 Incydr's *File Source Labeling* â€” inferring trust from **where a file came from / where it goes**, not its content â€” is the closest production analogue and is used here **correctly**: the push **destination** is ground truth, whereas session *intent* is something Incydr never claimed to classify ([Code42](https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20221019005695/en/Code42-Incydr-Automates-File-Source-Labeling-to-Elevate-Events-Involving-Sensitive-Business-Data)).

The signal set is sorted **by trustworthiness**, not by how much it costs to compute.

### 2.2 The cascade

**TIER G â€” GROUND TRUTH** *(the only signals that AUTO-resolve to WORK, confidence 0.95)*

| Signal | What it is | Why it is authoritative |
|---|---|---|
| **W-PUSH** | An actual git push whose destination remote matches a corporate org | The destination is the ground truth (Incydr analogue). Spoofing it requires push access to the corp org. |
| **W-IDP-EMAIL (signed)** | The **committer** identity on a commit **signed by an MDM/IdP-provisioned key**, matched server-side against the corporate IdP/SCIM directory | Survives the `--author` spoof. `git config --local user.email` is dev-mutable and **local always beats global** ([git-scm](https://git-scm.com/docs/git-config); [confirmed](https://devops.aibit.im/en/article/git-configuration-scopes-explained)), so an unsigned email is worth ~0 as governance. |

> **Residual-dissent fix adopted (hardening W-IDP-EMAIL):** auto-resolve to WORK only when the commit is **cryptographically signed** by a key provisioned through MDM/IdP enrollment *and* the verified committer identity matches the directory. **An unsigned author-email match is demoted to a Tier-C corroborator.** Ships with a **regression test asserting that `git commit --author="<spoofed corp email>"` on an *unsigned* commit does NOT produce an auto-WORK verdict.**

**Any one Tier-G signal â‡’ WORK 0.95, auto-resolved, not surfaced unless contested.**

---

**TIER C â€” CORROBORATORS** *(content-free, structural, injection-immune, but SPOOFABLE â€” never auto-resolve alone)*

- **C-MDM-ENV** â€” a corporate env var (e.g. `CORP_TENANT_ID`) injected by the **MDM-managed shell login profile**. Fires regardless of directory, **before any git op**, not spoofable without MDM access. *(W0/TPM attestation is explicitly NOT in the trust path: a local admin can present a software KSP as a TPM KSP ([Microsoft](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/security/hardware-security/tpm/tpm-fundamentals)), and devs often hold local admin â€” W0 is a soft hint only.)*
- **C-EMAIL-CFG** â€” `git config user.email` (honoring `includeIf`) resolves to a corporate domain. **Timing caveat, verified:** `includeIf "gitdir:"` needs `.git` to already exist, so it **does not fire in a bare folder before `git init`** ([git-scm](https://git-scm.com/docs/git-config); [vscode#40354](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/40354)); `hasconfig:remote.*.url` needs a remote. This is a **post-init hint, not a pre-init oracle.** Weight low.
- **C-REGISTRY** â€” private-registry fingerprint in walked-up manifests (`@org` npm scope, internal `registry=`, `GOPRIVATE`, internal Cargo index, Artifactory/CodeArtifact). Personal Verdaccio/GitHub Packages exist, so this is **not** zero-false-positive and **not** a hard override.
- **C-MONOREPO** â€” walk up (stop at the **first** `.git` boundary) to a workspace root whose **inherited remote matches a corporate org** (`pnpm-workspace.yaml`, `lerna.json`, `rush.json`, root `package.json#workspaces`).
- **C-TICKET** â€” **tenant-configured** issue-key regex (admin sets exact prefixes â€” not the broad `[A-Z]{2,}-\d+`) in branch/commit metadata.

**Rule: corroborators NEVER auto-resolve.** `â‰¥1 corroborator + no Tier-G â‡’ **WORK-PROVISIONAL**` (treated as work everywhere, flagged provisional, re-checked at SessionEnd / first push).

---

**TIER A â€” ADVISORY JUDGE** *(opt-in content tier â€” DEFERRED to v2)*

Built only after the **measured** residual-UNCLASSIFIED rate proves a real ambiguity problem. When built:
- Runs **async, on the company's own endpoint**, against a **structured policy schema** (typed predicates: `work_domains[]`, `work_ticket_prefixes[]`, `work_hours_window`, `approved_langs[]`) â€” **not admin prose**, which removes the prose injection surface.
- It can move a session **toward WORK or abstain to review**; it can **never** produce a PERSONAL-for-enforcement verdict. Spotlighting/guardrails are bypassable >90% under adaptive attack ([adaptive-attacks literature](https://arxiv.org/html/2504.11168v1)), so the **structural veto**, not the prompt defense, is load-bearing.
- Calibration uses a **conformal-prediction wrapper** (black-box, no logit access â€” works on Bedrock/Vertex endpoints where temperature scaling cannot, and gives finite-sample coverage without the 500â€“1000-label cold start isotonic needs). Raw LLM confidence is systematically overconfident and unusable as a gate ([ACL 2024](https://aclanthology.org/2024.findings-acl.357.pdf)). The classifier must abstain rather than label-force, which raw LLMs do badly ([arXiv 2406.16203](https://arxiv.org/html/2406.16203v1)).

### 2.3 Confidence model

- **Only Tier-G feeds an AUTO-resolve.** A pure sum of two Tier-C corroborators **cannot** reach auto-WORK â€” this kills the "corporate-checkout walk-up + stale env var = silent auto-work" spoof. Corroborator-only â‡’ **provisional + surfaced**, never silently classified.
- **No magic weights.** There is no asserted `35/30/25`. Thresholds are fit on a **labeled per-tenant holdout**; **until that holdout exists the system runs observation-only and shows confidence as a wide band.**
- **`UNCLASSIFIED` is a first-class terminal state**, not a fallback to personal. PERSONAL requires an affirmative personal signal *and* two independent confirmations (Â§4).

### 2.4 The hard edge case â€” new module, separate dir, no remote â€” resolves to WORK

Engineer opens a fresh folder outside the work tree, no git remote yet:

1. **MDM shell active â†’** `C-MDM-ENV` fires immediately, **pre-git â‡’ WORK-PROVISIONAL.**
2. **First commit â†’** if signed by the IdP-provisioned key, `W-IDP-EMAIL` checks server-side â‡’ **WORK 0.95 the moment they commit, no remote needed.**
3. **First push to the corp org â†’** `W-PUSH` â‡’ **WORK 0.95, permanent.**
4. **Truly bare (pre-commit, no MDM) â†’** the session is **UNCLASSIFIED â€” never personal** â€” because PERSONAL requires an affirmative personal signal and UNCLASSIFIED is excluded from every enforcement path.

> **Stated on the tin:** *"New/separate/remote-less work is never silently flagged personal."* This is structurally guaranteed by construction, not by a gameable email anchor.

### 2.5 Learning ledger (hardened)

Every admin review-ruling and every dev one-tap "this is work" writes an **append-only, attributed** `pattern_override` row (`scope device>user>tenant`, `predicate`, `reason â‰¤140 char`, `source`, `supersedes_id`).
- **Trust-but-verify:** a dev override **instantly clears the dev's own provisional label** (no manager gate) but enters **training weight only if independently corroborated** by a Tier-G/Tier-C signal. Uncorroborated dev labels stay soft and surface as *"dev-asserted, unverified."*
- **Anti-poisoning (concrete):** a `reclassify_rate > 2 SD above the tenant median over a rolling 30 days` â‡’ **quarantine for human review** (auditable, never auto-punish).
- **Staleness circuit-breaker:** every override carries `reviewed_at + staleness_after_days (default 180)`; stale overrides downgrade hard-pin â†’ soft-prior and re-queue (kills departed-employee ghost records).

### 2.6 Privacy posture (the load-bearing legal control)

- **Metadata-default; content is a deliberate opt-in tier.** CNIL/AEPD enforcement shows routine full-content capture for classification fails proportionality ([anonym.legal](https://anonym.legal/blog/aepd-spain-ai-dpia-gdpr-compliance-2025)). Tiers G+C are entirely structural and injection-immune; only the opt-in Tier-A judge reads content, in-tenancy.
- **Self-host keeps content in the company tenancy.** Anthropic's own Team plan already makes this boundary explicit (admins see metadata, not text; content access is an Enterprise/Compliance-API tier) ([aiopsschool](https://aiopsschool.com/blog/what-your-employer-can-see-on-claude-enterprise-a-complete-transparency-guide/)).
- **Dissent fix adopted â€” move file diffs + on-task score OUT of the metadata-default tier.** The proportionality-compliant default is: session existence, timing, model, token counts, the classification **verdict**, and the **structural signal booleans** (remote-host match, IdP-email match) â€” **NOT raw diffs, NOT a behavioural on-task score.** Diffs + on-task become a **strictly opt-in content tier** with its own notice/consent/works-council predicate.
- **Notice + acknowledgement ledger gates ALL collection (metadata included)**, parameterised by jurisdiction (NY/CT/DE conspicuous notice + on-hire acknowledgement; EU/DE worker information). A build-time gate **blocks the agent from collecting** until the tenant attests notice is posted (and, where required, acknowledgements captured). US notice statutes and the GDPR Art. 88/35 DPIA-before-monitoring duty are cited in the data sheet ([yaware state guide](https://yaware.com/blog/employee-monitoring-laws-by-state-2025-complete-guide/); [gdprlocal](https://gdprlocal.com/gdpr-employee-monitoring/)).

## 3. Humane Personal-Usage Limit

### 3.1 Denominator â€” recut to measurable reality

This is the dissent's fatal kill, and it is **fixed**:

- **DROP all per-session and per-seat DOLLAR caps.** The JSONL token fields are a streaming placeholder; ~75% of `input_tokens` entries are 0/1 and never finalized; input undercounted **100â€“174Ã—**, output **10â€“17Ã—** (ccusage measured **225k vs a real 10.4M â€” a 46Ã— gap**) ([gille.ai](https://gille.ai/en/blog/claude-code-jsonl-logs-undercount-tokens/); [#22686](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/22686); [ccusage#866](https://github.com/ryoppippi/ccusage/issues/866), [#888](https://github.com/ryoppippi/ccusage/issues/888)). **A dollar meter on this data is deleted.**
- **The only honest dollar unit** is **per-user-per-day from the Claude Enterprise Analytics / Compliance API**, lagged (refreshed ~4h, up to 24h, **native-Claude only â€” not Bedrock/Vertex**). No official API exposes per-session $. Dollars are therefore a **daily org/user rollup for the CFO dashboard, never a real-time gate.**
- **For personal-vs-work limiting the denominator is SESSION-COUNT or wall-clock fraction** â€” which Claresso *can* measure on-device â€” labeled **"estimated split, not billed dollars."** A **code-level lock forbids attaching a dollar figure to that split.** Net: *"personal â‰¤ 20% of **sessions**"* ships; *"â‰¤ 20% of **spend**"* is deleted.
- **Bedrock/Vertex seats are code-locked to `estimated == transparency-only`**, stated on the data sheet. (A premium CFO integration may *optionally* pull true cost from AWS Cost Explorer / GCP Billing for **cost allocation**, never as a real-time personal gate.)
- **UNCLASSIFIED is excluded from BOTH numerator and denominator** â€” invisible to the meter. The "convert after 30 days" idea is **removed entirely** for new/remote-less work (it is a **non-convertible terminal state by construction**). A **ballooning unclassified fraction is itself a review indicator** to the admin â€” human review, not an auto-debit.

### 3.2 Session-intent declaration (decoupled from enforcement)

One-click **"This session is [Work | Exploration | Other]"** injected once at the natural start boundary via `SessionStart` `additionalContext`. It informs the classifier label and the dev's **own** My-Activity view â€” but is **code-locked out of being any enforcing rung's numerator/denominator.** (If a declaration could debit an allowance it is coercive and devs would always Skip; **Skip = Unknown = excluded.**) This gives a defensible GDPR lawful basis (the dev actively contributes) and a durable prior-commitment mechanism **without post-hoc anchoring.**

### 3.3 Why the UX isn't crappy

The naive nag â€” *"you've spent too much on personal, switch to work"* â€” is exactly the design behavioral research warns against: hard blocks trigger psychological reactance and backfire, while **soft friction** (a brief deliberate pause) cuts unwanted behavior up to **57%** without resentment ([PNAS](https://www.pnas.org/doi/10.1073/pnas.2213114120)); **allowance framing** preserves agency where a "cap" creates a ceiling-as-floor threat ([behavioraleconomics.com](https://www.behavioraleconomics.com/the-budgeting-app-trap-when-spending-information-backfires/)); **developmental** monitoring (data returned to the employee) facilitates proactive behavior while **preventive** monitoring inhibits it, fully mediated by reactance ([ResearchGate](https://www.researchgate.net/publication/381961216)); and Apple Screen Time's adult UX is the cautionary tale of parental-control framing imposed on adults ([aibucket](https://www.aibucket.io/post/apple-faces-scrutiny-over-screen-time)).

> **Honesty note (not over-claimed):** the PNAS soft-friction and Screen-Time/RescueTime durability evidence comes from **opt-in, self-directed** contexts and does **not** transfer cleanly to **employer-imposed** friction. The honest v1 mechanism is **transparency + prior-commitment declaration + contestability**, not a behavioral guarantee.

The dev sees a resource they **co-own and can contest**, framed as **remaining headroom**, surfaced **before** any manager; correction is **one instant tap**; nobody is watched one-directionally; the worst v1 outcome is an ambient note.

### 3.4 The escalation ladder â€” v1 ships Rungs 0â€“1 ONLY

| Rung | Who sees it | Behavior |
|---|---|---|
| **0 â€” Transparency** (always on) | Dev | "My Activity" view: own work/personal/unclassified split + contestable ledger. The **same cohort aggregate the admin sees** (reciprocal, common-knowledge policy panel â€” **not** a ranked leaderboard; imposed gamification triggers reactance/cheating). Optional ambient `statusLine` chip is **best-effort**: renders only after workspace-trust, shows a **cached** session-start value, **never blocks input**. |
| **1 â€” Dev-only nudge** (~80%) | Dev only | Non-blocking `systemMessage` at a natural idle, **no manager ping**, with one-tap "this is work." |
| **Manager visibility** | Manager | **Never** an individual drill-down without a **deliberate, logged action that notifies the employee.** Until precision clears the contractual floor, managers see only **"unclassified, excluded"** and raw activity counts â€” **never a personal-share percentage.** |

> **Product-wide failing-build invariant (named surfaces):** *"the dev sees their own number before any manager aggregate"* and *"no manager individual drill-down without a logged, employee-notifying action"* must hold for **every** per-engineer surface: classifier label, limiter split, **on-task score, secrets/PII findings, session-replay, eDiscovery search.** A guarantee that protects one window and silently exempts replay/eDiscovery is not the guarantee.

### 3.5 If/when to hard-block â€” NOT v1; off-device proxy only

On-device hooks **cannot reliably enforce.** Confirmed: managed/`settings.json` `deny` rules are ignored for Read/Write in multiple builds ([#6631](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/6631), [#8961](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/8961), [#27040](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/27040)), and `allow` rules are themselves intermittently ignored ([#18160](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/18160)). Anthropic's *documented intent* is that managed-settings `deny` is absolute and evaluated regardless of a `PreToolUse` hook return ([Configure permissions](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permissions)) â€” but the live enforcement bugs above mean **you cannot rely on the hook surface to block.** Model-downgrade-via-hook is undocumented and architecturally needs a proxy anyway.

Hard-block is therefore allowed **only**:
- **(a)** via the **separately-priced, separately-deployed off-device API proxy** that can meter in real time and substitute models;
- **(b)** only on a session a **Tier-G or two-independent-signal** check confirms personal â€” **never on UNCLASSIFIED, never on single-work-signal** (an AUP-published, tested invariant);
- **(c)** only after a **build-time GO/NO-GO** proves PERSONAL-class precision (false-personal rate on **â‰¥200â€“500 stratified human-confirmed work labels per tenant** below an agreed numeric floor) â€” **code-locked off until met**;
- **(d)** only with a **named human reviewer in the loop** (Art. 22 safeguard) and a **warm, contactable, one-click-recoverable** message â€” never a silent refusal, never a mid-flight kill, **only gating the START of a new confirmed-personal session**;
- **(e)** defense-in-depth: a `SessionStart` `additionalContext` note may *ask* the model to self-decline personal tool calls â€” advisory, never the sole primitive.

Even on the proxy, every enforcing hook is **pinned to an allowlist of Claude Code versions that pass a runtime precedence self-test**; the deny-bypass bugs are kept as **regression tests**; if the self-test fails or the CC version is outside the tested matrix, enforcement **FAILS CLOSED** (auto-disables; transparency continues). A **proxy outage can never block the developer's coding tool** (written fail-open guarantee).

## 4. How the two halves work together

One pipeline, joined at **three hard contracts**, so limiting can never punish a misclassification.

**1 â€” Shared trust tiers, one direction of safety.** The classifier's Tier-G / Tier-C / UNCLASSIFIED states **are** the limiter's gates. The limiter consumes only the safe side: a session counts toward "personal share" **only if it carries an affirmative personal signal AND is confirmed by two independent signals** (inclusionary *"confirm work, else unknown"* model). UNCLASSIFIED and single-work-signal sessions can **never** trip any rung and aggregate to a manager only as *"unclassified, excluded."* â€” a tested, AUP-published invariant.

> **"Two independent signals" defined concretely:** two signals from **distinct, non-derivable provenance classes**. `push-destination`, `IdP-commit-email`, and `MDM-env` are independent; **`no remote` + `non-corp git email` are NOT** (both derive from "working outside the corp checkout"). A test **rejects a PERSONAL verdict built from correlated signals**, and the independence taxonomy is **published in the AUP** so the headline invariant is falsifiable.

**2 â€” The edge case flows through safely by construction.** The new-module session resolves to WORK (via `C-MDM-ENV` pre-git â†’ `W-IDP-EMAIL` on commit â†’ `W-PUSH` on push) or, if truly bare, sits UNCLASSIFIED. In **every** branch it is excluded from the personal denominator and cannot be blocked/throttled. Its spend appears only in the daily CFO rollup, never as "personal." **"New = punished" is impossible regardless of which half you look at.**

**3 â€” The ledger is the single contestable surface for both.** The one-tap "this is work" both reclassifies (classifier) and clears the dev's provisional personal share (limiter), instantly, dev-first, logged, **no manager gate** â€” satisfying the Art. 22 right-to-contest **once** for both problems. The same `>2 SD` contradict-guard protects both the classifier's training weight and the limiter's denominator, while staying an **indicator-for-review, never an auto-sanction.**

## 5. Build notes â€” the real Rust / Postgres / managed-settings stack

**Signal collection** â€” `ccguard-core` Rust collector at `SessionStart`/`SessionEnd` hooks; `cwd`, `transcript_path`, `session_id` are in the hook contract. C-MDM-ENV reads the injected env var; C-EMAIL-CFG/C-REGISTRY/C-MONOREPO/C-TICKET are file/`git`-walk reads from `cwd` up to the first `.git` boundary. **No content is read in Tiers G/C.**

**Server-side ground truth** â€” commit-signature + committer-identity-vs-IdP check at **push** (and at first signed commit), done **server-side from the recorded commit object**, never from `git config`.

**Postgres schema (sketch):**
- `session_signals` â€” append-only `(session_id, signal_code, tier, value, source, observed_at)`
- `session_classification` â€” `(session_id, verdict, confidence_lo, confidence_hi, resolved_by, resolved_at, provisional bool)`
- `pattern_override` â€” `(id, scope, predicate, reason â‰¤140, source, supersedes_id, reviewed_at, staleness_after_days, corroborated bool)`
- `enforcement_arming` â€” `(tenant, seat, rung, armed bool, go_decision_id, measured_precision, fail_closed_state, dated)` â€” surfaced to the **dev's own** My-Activity view so the dev can verify *"no rung is armed against me; observation-only since <date>"* as a first-class fact, not a vendor assurance.

**Limiter unit** â€” rolling **7-day** session-count / wall-clock fraction, aligned to Anthropic's weekly reset cadence ([usage limits](https://support.claude.com/en/articles/11647753-how-do-usage-and-length-limits-work)). A **code-level lock** forbids binding a dollar figure to the personal/work split; the dollar rollup is a **separate** daily Enterprise-Analytics ingest, native-Claude only.

**On-device surfaces** â€” `statusLine` chip (cached, non-blocking), `systemMessage` nudge, `SessionStart` `additionalContext` intent declaration. **No enforcing hook ships in v1.**

**Enforcement (later SKU)** â€” off-device API proxy, version-pinned, runtime precedence self-test, **fail-closed**, with the [#6631/#8961/#27040/#18160](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/27040) deny-bypass cases kept as regression tests.

**Self-host** â€” the whole Tier-G/C pipeline + optional Tier-A judge run **inside the customer's infrastructure**; the classifier model (if/when Tier-A ships) is a versioned ONNX artifact shipped with the agent; **no customer data leaves to train any base model.**

## 6. Open questions & risks

1. **Sandbagging is a first-class, signed line item** â€” not a footnote. The contract and data sheet must state that a motivated insider configuring their environment to look like work is **probabilistically detectable but NOT prevented**, and that Claresso must **never** be represented (internally, to regulators, or to works councils) as a **definitive** measure of personal-vs-work use. This protects the buyer in the inevitable disputed case.
2. **Reference-tenant evaluation before ANY production deployment (including observation-only).** Publish a classifier eval on a **human-labeled, stratified holdout** covering the hard stacks (no-remote shell/Jupyter, Go-no-modules, IaC, monorepo-no-leaf-remote): report **PERSONAL-class precision, false-WORK, and false-PERSONAL rates with confidence intervals.** Code-lock the manager-visible personal-share aggregate **OFF** until precision clears a contractually agreed floor.
3. **EU is build-time-gated on the CLASSIFIER, not just the limiter.** A failing-build test must prove that with geo/tenant = EU (or DE/AT) and **no signed Betriebsvereinbarung on file, ZERO signal collection occurs** â€” including the observation month and all metadata â€” and limiter enforcement paths are unreachable. EU works councils in DE/NL/AT hold a genuine **blocking veto** over behaviour-monitoring systems ([HewardMills](https://www.hewardmills.com/works-councils-and-data-privacy-rights/)). **Outside-counsel must answer GO** on the binary question â€” *"is a work/personal classification informing a manager review queue itself Annex-III high-risk worker-behaviour evaluation?"* â€” **before any EU tenant sees a classification surface.** If yes-high-risk, ship in EU only after deployer-side Art. 26 duties (worker-rep consultation + employee information + FRIA) are satisfied per tenant.
4. **Art. 22 non-determinativeness as a tested control, not prose:** (a) manager surface shows aggregate-by-default; any drill-down is logged, employee-notified, and records the reviewer's **independent rationale that does not merely echo the score**; (b) audited prohibition on using Claresso output as the **sole/primary** basis for any HR adverse action, in the AUP + DPA; (c) **DPO sign-off per tenant** that the human-review loop clears "solely automated" under the SCHUFA standard before any individual-level surface is enabled.
5. **On-task score + job-role anomaly indicators** (`non_engineer_coding`, etc.) are bound to the **exact same** guarantees as the classifier (dev-sees-own-first, logged/notified drill-down, one-tap contest into the same ledger, EU build-time disable). **If they cannot meet these, they are feature-flagged OFF** in any tenant where the classifier/limiter ships â€” so they can't become the un-contestable behaviour verdict the classifier was built not to be.
6. **Retention + purpose-limitation + DPIA + deletion-on-exit spine:** short tiered default retention (raw signals â‰¤ N days, aggregates longer, content-tier shortest); a **code-enforced purpose-limitation tag** binding classification output to **governance use only** (blocking export to performance-management systems without a separate logged consent + works-council step); a shipped **tenant DPIA template**; a **hard delete-on-departure** routine (which also resolves the stale-override ghost-record risk). The Betriebsvereinbarung gate enforces these as its **minimum content**, not a bare signature check.
7. **Proxy architecture spec is a precondition to selling enforcement:** written latency/availability/failure-mode analysis + the **fail-open guarantee** (a proxy outage cannot block coding) must exist **before** the enforcement SKU is offered.
8. **LLM-judge cost/latency reality** (if Tier-A is ever built): per-event frontier-API classification is uneconomic (~$4k/yr for 100 seats) and slow ([arXiv pricing](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2602.06370)); the in-tenancy path is a small on-prem encoder/vLLM, async and advisory only ([Red Hat vLLM](https://developers.redhat.com/articles/2025/08/08/ollama-vs-vllm-deep-dive-performance-benchmarking)) â€” **never a real-time gate.**
